# OpenMaterials

> OpenMaterials is a versioned, content-addressed map of physical quantities and formulas. Simulated and measured values attach to it with their provenance. Data is CC BY 4.0 and code is Apache 2.0. OpenMaterials is stewarded by OpenMaterials-AI, a foundation in formation.

Cite the map version in https://openmaterials.ai/data/version.json with any value you reuse.

## Data

- [graph.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/graph.json): typed quantities, the links between them with operators and formulas, and the tiers
- [catalog.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/catalog.json): symbol, dimension, and description per node
- [codes.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/codes.json): each code's representation, citation, and license
- [semantics.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/semantics.json): the labels per node and edge that the resolver matches
- [instances.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/instances.json): committed values with their provenance
- [lean.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/lean.json): each node's dimension as a Physlib seven-base ISQ declaration in the single Lean package, with its Physlib revision and toolchain
- [formula_bindings.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/formula_bindings.json): Physlib mappings at a pinned revision, scientific identities, assumptions, and remaining proof obligations; source links are not compiled equivalence proofs
- [physlib_dimensions.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/physlib_dimensions.json): seven-base ISQ dimensions for catalog fields, with opaque fields excluded; dimension checks do not establish formula equivalence
- [version.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/version.json): map version, graph version, and genesis hash

## Docs

- [Guide](https://openmaterials.ai/guide/): install the omai kernel, resolve a label, load the graph, and parse a paper
- [Document](https://openmaterials.ai/document/): the full specification, also as [PDF](https://openmaterials.ai/openmaterials.pdf)
- [Codes](https://openmaterials.ai/codes/): the bibliography of the codes the map cites; each code has a landing page at /codes/<key>/ (what it is, what it computes, references, embedded map)
- [Data contract](https://openmaterials.ai/guide/#data): the shapes of the main JSON files under data/
- [Repository](https://github.com/openmaterials-ai/openmaterials-ai): source, GOVERNANCE.md, and the contribution process
- [Formula bridge](https://openmaterials.ai/lean/bridge/): mapping coverage and gaps. Physlib-anchored proofs cover the harmonic ensembles, the static-plus-harmonic Cp and thermal Gruneisen identities, the quasiharmonic Gibbs, C_P, expansion, modulus and Gruneisen-contraction producers, crystal lattice dynamics (dynamical matrix, commensurate dispersion, group velocity away from Gamma) and the relaxation-time conductivity; local proofs over Mathlib cover elastic moduli, composite conductivity and cure kinetics. Compiled model proofs do not verify numerical producers. The non-analytic correction, the linearized-BTE collision matrix and the linearized-BTE cumulative conductivity are recorded as catalog defects. It is the map's only Lean package.

## Values

- A committed value's id is the SHA-256 hash of its lineage object: 64 lowercase hex characters, the id field in instances.json.
- The datasheet for a value opens at https://openmaterials.ai/play/#id={id}; a prefix of 8 or more hex characters also resolves.
- https://openmaterials.ai/i/{id}/ is the value's permalink: it carries a preview card for link unfurls and opens the datasheet.
- Short links of the form https://openmaterials.ai/l/{prefix} open the same datasheet; the prefix is 8 or more hex characters of the id, and the site prints 12.

## Optional

- [Playground](https://openmaterials.ai/play/): parse a paper, open a lineage record, or resolve a method name
- [Map](https://openmaterials.ai/map/) and [Map in 3D](https://openmaterials.ai/map-3d/)
- [lean_roadmap.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/lean_roadmap.json): one row per operator, rated by what a Lean proof of its formula would take
- [agreement.json](https://openmaterials.ai/data/agreement.json): the comparison groups and their spread
- [Run a calculation](https://materialscodegraph.com/?ref=omai-llms#hero-connect): MaterialsCodeGraph, from Da Vinci Labs, runs these calculations for AI agents over MCP, with a binding token quote before every run and a permanent record after it.
